aliases.$comment: Hand-written ABI slices in app/src, and the deployed contracts each one addresses. A slice is a real UI path -- useVaultsSummary declares a three-fragment vault ABI because the full one trips TS2589 -- but nothing in the file says which contract it speaks to, so it is said here. One entry is not a slice but another contract's GENERATED binding: the four alignment vaults all implement IAlignmentVault, and useVaultOverview reads the shared selectors (vaultType, accumulatedFees, totalShares) off ANY vault through the endowment family's hooks rather than generating three more bindings for identical selectors. The call is real and the address is the LP vault's, so the credit belongs to the LP vault.

skip.$comment: --- the alignment vault's benefactor surface: every benefactor is a collection instance, never a wallet ---

skip.why: The vault pays a BENEFACTOR, and a benefactor is always a collection instance: the liquidity deployer modules register `p.instance` at graduation and the ERC-1155/721 instances register `address(this)` on every tithe. `msg.sender` is the benefactor here, so a wallet calling it holds no shares and reverts `NoShares`. The creator's path runs through their own instance -- `claimVaultFees` / `claimAllFees`, which every per-type admin panel offers and which forward the proceeds to the owner. The endowment family implements the selector by reverting `NotSupported`: it has no tradable shares, and its claim is `claimYieldPurse`, which the collection's vault panel calls.

A delegate's batch claim across several benefactors. Only a benefactor may appoint a delegate (`delegateBenefactor`), and no benefactor is a wallet, so nothing in this deployment can appoint one and no address can be a delegate.

Appoints who receives a benefactor's payouts. `msg.sender` must already be a benefactor -- a collection instance -- and no instance forwards this call, so the delegation surface has no caller. The endowment reverts `NotSupported` outright. See claimFees.
The read paired with delegateBenefactor. Nothing can appoint a delegate here, so it answers the benefactor's own address for every benefactor.

The interface's claimable read, keyed by benefactor -- a collection instance. On the liquidity families it reports only what has already been crystallized into the fee accumulator: `claimFees` collects the position's new pool fees FIRST and pays more than this. Printed beside a creator's claim button it would under-quote their own money, which is worse than printing nothing. The endowment's equivalent is exact, and is the `pendingYieldOf` the vault panel shows.
Uni's own name for calculateClaimableAmount -- the two compute the same expression against the same watermark. See calculateClaimableAmount.

How much ETH one collection has tithed into this vault over its life. It buys the collection its share of the split, and the share is what pays; the figure a creator acts on is the claim their admin panel offers, not the basis behind it.

One collection's share of the vault's fee split. The vault page reports `totalShares`, which says how many claimants the pool is divided between; the per-collection slice is the ledger behind a claim rather than a number anyone acts on.
The storage mapping behind getBenefactorContribution. See it.
Uni's storage mapping behind getBenefactorContribution. See it.
The storage mapping behind getBenefactorShares. See it.
The storage mapping behind getBenefactorDelegate. See it.
The storage mapping behind `principalOf`, which the collection's vault panel reads to show its pre-vest principal.
The storage mapping behind `vestedOf` -- principal that has already moved into the target's deployable corpus.

The SETTLED half of a benefactor's claimable creator yield. `pendingYieldOf`, which the vault panel reads, returns it plus the accrual not yet settled into it -- the figure the claim actually pays, and the only one worth showing.
The MasterChef accumulator's per-benefactor watermark: the bookkeeping that makes a claim pay the delta rather than the lifetime total. It is not a quantity anyone holds.
When a benefactor last claimed. Recorded for the accumulator's own audit trail; nothing in the payout depends on it and no surface counts down from it.
The IAlignmentVault policy hook. Every family in this deployment returns empty bytes -- no vault carries a policy, so there is nothing for a surface to render.

An arbitrary external call spending up to the target's vested corpus, authorised to the ambassador of a curated target. That is sovereign capital, and the ambassador panel says so at the point where it declines to offer it: a web build that can make this call is one stolen build artifact away from making it. De-curating the target freezes the power, and `releaseCorpusToCommunity` is the corpus's exit that survives.
The validator's quote, called by the vault inside its own swap to floor the caller's `minOut`. Its caller is a vault, and what a user sees is the price that passed it.
How much of a pending balance to swap so both legs of an LP add are covered. Arithmetic the vault performs on itself, mid-transaction.

The vault an instance was CREATED with, kept so the revenue split can stay keyed to the family it was launched under even after a migration. The app reads the instance's current `vault` and the registry's vault list; which one was first is a fact for the split, not for a reader.
